findings.body: The protected compact layout is created only when an active item exists (line 86), and the other protected count layout excludes narrow strips (line 96). With lane data but no active item, a 79-column strip therefore reaches this fallback, placing its counts in a truncatable prefix beside an unrestricted command button. A long runnable command, such as the one already used by the compact-layout test, can displace the required counts. This is a sibling case the previous rulings did not weigh: the new tests always supply active items. Reserve the count cells and constrain the trailing command even when there is no active item.

findings.body: The older-Forge case presses the next-step button but never checks that a prompt was submitted. Its prompt.submit interception at line 129 records nothing; subsequent assertions only inspect the drawing and hotkey property. A handler that returns immediately whenever lane data is absent would pass this case and all submission assertions in the other test, which supplies lanes. Record submissions and assert the exact command after pressing in the older-Forge state, as detail 2 explicitly requires.
